title: Missed observability signals and runbook for dashboard query timeouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During the 2025-02-07 console slow incident (INC-2025-02-07-CONSOLE-SLOW) we discovered multiple blind spots that delayed root-cause identification and remediation. Key failures: several Grafana dashboards were returning stale or timed-out queries under load, important per-tenant ingestion and request-size distribution metrics did not exist, and tracing correlated IDs were not propagated from the console frontend to backend runtime requests. Combined, these gaps masked queuing pressure and KV cache eviction correlation with long-tail latency and led to firefighting focused on the wrong subsystem for ~45 minutes.

Why this is a problem:
- Without per-tenant ingestion_rate and request_size_histogram we cannot identify hot tenants or shifts in request profile that trigger autoscale or cache thrash.
- Dashboard queries timing out/returning partial results hide early signals; we had no reliable alert that a dashboard had failed to execute its query due to resource saturation.
- Missing trace propagation meant we couldn't join console traces to runtime traces; diagnosing end-to-end tail latency required manual log gymnastics.

Goal:
Make these observability signals reliable and actionable so that future incidents are detected earlier, ownership is clear, and runbooks surface the correct remediation steps automatically.
acceptance_criteria: Add and backfill per-tenant ingestion_rate metric and request_size_histogram (labels: tenant_id, route)
Add a dashboard-level health metric: grafana_query_success{dashboard_id} and alert when success_rate < 95% over 5m
Propagate correlation_id from console frontend through API gateway to runtime and surface it in traces/logs
Update console runbook to include steps for diagnosing dashboard query timeouts and mapping tenant ingestion spikes to autoscale events
End-to-end test that simulates dashboard query timeouts under controlled load and verifies alerting and runbook steps
action_items: ENG: instrument metric: 'console.ingestion_rate_per_tenant' (owner: Luis Ortega) - add counter with tenant_id label and route label - due 2025-02-28
ENG: add 'console.request_size_histogram' metric and backfill 7 days from logs (owner: Priya Singh) - due 2025-02-26
ENG: add Grafana internal health metric 'grafana.query_success' and the dashboard health panel; create alert 'DashboardQueriesDown' (owner: Observability infra team) - due 2025-02-24
ENG: implement correlation_id propagation: frontend X-Redwood-Correlation header -> API gateway -> runtime logs/traces; add tests and update SDKs (owner: Luis Ortega) - due 2025-03-05
ENG: modify sampling policy to keep 100% traces for requests that hit slow-responding dashboards for 48 hours after deployment of health metric (owner: Observability infra) - due 2025-02-28
DOCS: update console incident runbook with new troubleshooting steps and example queries, link to example dashboard and alert play (owner: Maya Chen) - due 2025-02-22
QA: create a chaos test that times out dashboard queries under load and verifies 'DashboardQueriesDown' fires and playbook guides operator to root cause (owner: QA Reliability) - due 2025-03-01
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Triage notes from postmortem meeting. Primary driver appears to be a tenant that increased average request size 4x after a client-side change. We lacked per-tenant metrics so correlation was manual.

2025-02-13 Luis Ortega: Started a spike to evaluate where to add ingestion counters. Thinking to add at the API gateway ingress and also at the console proxy layer to capture different perspectives. Will PR schema changes for metrics next week.

2025-02-15 Priya Singh: Found that request body size is already emitted at the runtime, but not aggregated in Prometheus. Plan: add a histogram aggregation and a nightly backfill job that scans logs to populate histogram buckets for the last 7 days.

2025-02-17 Observability infra: We can expose grafana.query_success via the Grafana backend plugin. Will prototype and add dashboard health panels. Note: need to ensure alerting noise is limited (thresholds and silences).

2025-02-18 PM review (Jordan Blake): Prioritize correlation_id propagation first — root-cause workflows were most impacted by missing traces. Agreed to triage other items into next sprint if blockers appear.

2025-02-20 Luis Ortega: Implemented initial metric naming and submitted PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/438. Metrics are behind a feature flag and include tenant_id label. Next: add dashboards and alerts.
notes: This ticket focuses on measurable signal additions and concrete runbook improvements rather than UI polish. Coordinate with SRE and runtime teams for metric contracts and cost implications of high-cardinality labels.
